result.note: Tests the FATF's mandate and leadership change, India's 2024 Mutual Evaluation tier, and FIU-IND's role.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, Vivek Aggarwal was appointed India's first-ever vice-president of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF). Consider the following statements:
items: The FATF is a Paris-based intergovernmental body that sets global standards on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing.
Aggarwal succeeds Giles Thomson of the UK, who becomes FATF president from 1 July 2026.
Aggarwal's term as vice-president runs from July 2026 to June 2028.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because Aggarwal holds the role from July 2026 to June 2027. Thomson's presidency is expected to focus on payment transparency and underground banking.
questions.source: Aggarwal holds the role from July 2026 to June 2027, succeeding Giles Thomson of the UK, who moves up to the FATF presidency from 1 July 2026.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's 2024 FATF Mutual Evaluation:
items: It placed India in the "regular follow-up" category, the FATF's highest rating tier.
India was the only G20 country placed in this tier.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the tier is shared by four other G20 countries. The story says this result laid the credibility foundation for Aggarwal's appointment as FATF vice-president in June 2026.
questions.source: The 2024 assessment placed India in the "regular follow-up" category, the FATF's highest rating tier, shared by only four other G20 countries.

questions.prompt: Vivek Aggarwal, appointed India's first FATF vice-president in June 2026, is a former head of which agency, India's central agency for tracking suspicious financial transactions?
questions.explain: Aggarwal previously headed FIU-IND, India's central agency for tracking suspicious financial transactions. He currently serves as Secretary at the Ministry of Culture.
questions.source: is a former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND), India's central agency for tracking suspicious financial transactions
